page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 32 vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core) on dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU), and features 1888 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage alongside support for Premium Storage. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-core capabilities, placing stress-ng single-core compute performance within the top 10% tier. Instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 contribute to top-tier execution in single-threaded gzip compression (41.23 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.08 GB/sec). PassMark evaluations also reflect strong overall CPU execution (57,509.96) and cryptographic performance (40,124.54), supported by hardware AES and VAES acceleration.

Multi-core execution and I/O throughput reside primarily in the middle 50% tier, with multi-core stress-ng registering 60,013.36 and PassMark database operations reaching 19,363.0. Memory bandwidth remains solid with 101.21 GB/sec uncached read and 67.44 GB/sec write on large 256 MB blocks. For AI inference tasks without a GPU, the instance achieves top-tier generation speeds of 413.11 tokens/sec on lightweight 135M parameter models, but falls back to middle-tier throughput (24.24 tokens/sec) on medium 7B models.

The D32ads_v7 offers balanced resource density and high single-threaded efficiency paired with fast local NVMe capacity. It is well-suited for general-purpose workloads that benefit from responsive single-core performance and fast scratch storage, such as high-traffic web applications, database staging, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and lightweight CPU-based inference services.
